NOTE: (1) The bedroom requirements are based on family composition. 
(2)  a. The displaced ability to pay has been computed as the gross rent of not more than 25% of gross income. 
 b. The purchase prices have been determined as being 2-1/2 times the gross income.
 c. In lieu of specific information, but based upon statements by the displacee of either admitted assets or an amount of compensation realized from the acquisition of the displacee's property, the amount shown for rent or for purchase was estimated taking into consideration age and recurring income.
The rehousing requirements from Table 1 are, in turn, shown statistically in the following Table 2, together with the current availability by price ranges. The area searched for current availability is bounded by Lincoln Avenue on the north to Ryan Road on the south and from Lake Michigan on the east to approximately 84th Street on the west. This area contains approximately 100,000 dwelling units.
Table 2 shows up two problem situations that are discussed later under the heading of "Potential Problems". These are the apparent need for a three-bedroom unit for under $80 and the four-bedroom unit at $130 per month. The availabilities for all other rental needs are expected to be adequate during the displacement period estimated at 12 months. This availability is further substantiated when consideration is given to the turnover in the area of like dwelling units. This turnover is shown in the following Table 3 which was tabulated for the past 3-month period. To be representative of the rental availability for a 12-month period, the figures shown would be multiplied by four.
